title: The Solar System
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: The Solar System Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Identify the Sun, planets, moons, asteroids and comets in the solar system; describe their properties and distances; describe stars, constellations and galaxies. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 science worksheets on the Sun, the eight planets, orbits, distances, stars, constellations and light years. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Rocky inner planets, gas and ice giants further out, all held in orbit by the Sun's gravity.
body_html:
How to think about it

Our solar system is the Sun and everything that orbits it.

  • Planets in order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
  • The inner planets are rocky; the outer planets are giants of gas and ice.
  • Stars make their own light. Constellations are star patterns; galaxies hold billions of stars.
Example

Which planet comes after Mars?

the order: … Earth, Mars, Jupiter

Answer: Jupiter

Example

Why do planets further out take longer to orbit?

longer path

slower speed

Answer: they have a longer year

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Moon and planets make their own light.
  • Thinking the Sun is the biggest star.
  • Thinking a light year is a unit of time.

items.q: Which planets are rocky (terrestrial)?
items.e: The four inner planets are rocky.

items.q: Which planet is next in from Mars, closer to the Sun?
items.e: Order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

items.q: What kind of planet is Uranus?
